html:
EOKA, the National Organisation of Cypriot Fighters, was a Greek Cypriot guerrilla group that fought British rule from 1955 to 1959 to unite Cyprus with Greece.

It was led by Georgios Grivas, a Cypriot born colonel of the Greek army, with the blessing of Archbishop Makarios. It began with bombs on 1 April 1955 and went on to ambushes and killings of soldiers, police and Greek Cypriots seen as traitors. Britain exiled Makarios to the Seychelles. Turkish Cypriots formed their own group, and the conflict turned between the communities. The struggle ended with the Zurich and London agreements, which made Cyprus an independent state rather than part of Greece.
sum: EOKA, the National Organisation of Cypriot Fighters, was a Greek Cypriot guerrilla group that fought British rule from 1955 to 1959 to unite Cyprus with Greece.
